details:
When a VR user attempts to point at a collider with interact event using their raycaster, it is near impossible for them to be able to highlight the interact, and use it.
This seem's to be caused due to how VRChat's VR raycaster interacts with GameObject Layers.
When the VR raycaster attempts to raycast, it will register a hit with a gameobject collider on any layer, even if the collider is marked as "Is Trigger", stopping the raycaster from raycasting any further. The only layer that the VR Raycaster does not hit is "MirrorReflection", and can be used as a workaround, though putting the trigger's object on this layer makes it not render in the player's view, unless they're rendering it from a mirror.
The problem with this for World Creators is that they are unable to have players be within a trigger collider, and use Interacts within them. This is a problem with things for example like a trigger detection system to toggle a mirror, but also having a button to override the toggle next to the mirror. A player needs to stand in the detection trigger to press the button, however due to their raycaster being blocked by the detection trigger they're standing within, they are unable to press the button. 
Detection triggers are a simple yet powerful way in game design to make events happen when the player enters, exits, or is within them. The "Mirror Reflection" layer workaround is not documented and not well known (I had to figure it out myself through trial and error), meaning most world creators have to come up with more complicated, inefficient workarounds. World creators should not have to find complicated workarounds, that take forever to set up, and that could end up being more performance intensive.
The VR raycaster should be fixed so that "Is Trigger" colliders do not interfere with it. If this is not possible due to limitations of the Unity Engine, there should at least be consideration on how this could be fixed.
title: Interact triggers are inoperable in VR while inside a larger trigger volume
